# Från hummer till The Weeknd – okända tillgångsslaget lockar

**Feed**: borslunch  
**Published**: 2026-11-27  
**Market Sentiment**: Positive

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Börslunch episode is mostly an interview with Stephen Otter, head of royalties at Partners Group. He presents royalties (music, film, healthcare, gas wells, YouTube, lobster) as an uncorrelated asset class driven by consumption that holds up in volatile markets. News segments describe a broad Stockholm rally led by miners and defence stocks. Swedish household confidence from Konjunkturinstitutet came in weak, Intrum rose after its Norwegian major owner bought shares, and the market reaction to SKF's Vertevo spin-off and Prisjakt's first report was mixed.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟠 SKF-B — SKF | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 40%

Stock recovered after the Vertevo spin-off; managers say they want the remaining quality SKF business.

#### Reasoning

Reporter Alexander Klaar notes that SKF shareholders effectively got Vertevo for free. Many managers prefer the core SKF that remains, which suggests positioning favours the parent over the automotive spin-off. This is commentary, not a recommendation.

#### Sell Triggers

- if core SKF guidance weakens
- if spin-off selling pressure spills over to the parent

> *"En frontad avknoppning där många förvaltare sagt Man vill åt det fina i SKF som kommer att bli kvar."*

---

### 🟠 INTRUM — Intrum | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 40%

Heavily shorted stock up ~7% after its Norwegian major owner bought shares again.

#### Reasoning

Insider and major-owner buying in a heavily shorted name can trigger a short squeeze. The reporter only states the fact, with no explicit recommendation, so this is a speculative watch.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the major owner stops buying
- if short interest builds further

> *"Kortpressade kredithanteraren Intrum upp 7 % ungefär efter att bolagets norska storägare köpt aktier igen."*
